headline: Geometry-aware representations guide estimation in biophysical and metabolic models
label: Geometry Aware Computational Modelling
summary: Recent preprints treat the geometry of modelled objects, such as cell shape, binding pockets, and isotopologue space, as central to inference.
synthesis: The three preprints share an attention to the geometry of the quantities being estimated before inference is performed. A theoretical 3D biophysical model links purse-string wound closure efficiency to cell aspect ratio, with very squamous tissues requiring substantially stronger contraction. A workflow applying the measure volinterior fuzzy-boundary algorithm is developed and validated for dynamic binding pockets at the HBV capsid assembly modulator site. Compositional I-MFA applies an ILR transformation to isotopologue distributions to reduce Euclidean bias, reporting 42.6% lower MSE in flux estimation. What is new is treating the representation space itself as part of the inference problem. The thread is not uniform: the wound-closure study is a mechanistic model rather than an estimation method, and each methodological claim currently rests on a single preprint.
